issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Ride.abbreviation as type String (problem_statement.md: Ride class shows "-abbreviation: String"), but the solution implements Ride.abbreviation as a char (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java: line declaring "private char abbreviation"). This mismatch propagates to all subclasses and constructors/getters (e.g. LaunchedRollerCoaster and LaunchedDropdownTower constructors accept a char abbreviation in the solution). The exercise instructions require students to implement attributes and constructors exactly as in the UML; following the UML (String) will produce code that differs from the provided solution and likely fail any tests expecting the solution's char-based signatures.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the type of Ride.abbreviation consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the UML and problem statement to declare abbreviation as a char (and mention that getters/constructors use char), or (B) change the solution (and any tests) so Ride.abbreviation is a String and adjust all constructors/getters/subclasses accordingly. Ensure the template (Ride.java) includes the same attribute type/signature to guide students.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Ride.abbreviation as type String, but the solution uses a char for the abbreviation attribute and constructor parameters (Ride.abbreviation: char, and subclasses' constructors take char). This type mismatch (String vs. char) creates an unintended naming/typing inconsistency: students following the UML will implement constructors/getters accepting/returning String while the solution/template code expects char (and vice versa), causing confusion about the correct attribute type and constructor signatures.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the abbreviation type consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement UML to declare abbreviation: char, or (B) change the solution (and template) to use String for Ride.abbreviation and update all constructors and getters to accept/return String (e.g., private String abbreviation; public Ride(String name, String abbreviation); subclasses' constructors call super(name, abbreviation)). Prefer updating the solution/template to match the UML (String) unless the course intends abbreviation to be a single character, in which case update the UML to char to avoid student confusion.
